description: Pierce County Planning and Public Works publishes GPS-located end points where stormwater leaves engineered drainage systems and enters natural systems such as streams or rivers. The layer covers unincorporated Pierce County, Washington. Its native metadata defines point geometry, asset identifiers, end-point type, receiving destination, elevation, maintenance group and survey-date fields. The inventory can support the representation of drainage outlets and receiving-water connections in network-flow studies. The metadata does not establish discharge rates, hydraulic capacity or the completeness of all outlets. The public Socrata table is accessible through the county catalogue, with field definitions exposed in API metadata. The source refers users to county terms of use; a standard licence is not established in this review. Individual values and geometry were not inspected. The related drainage break-point record describes directional changes within channels, which differ from these discharge locations.
